turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Morning, Kim. Quick heads-up — I pointed DNS at the new cluster before it was fully ready. I thought it would be fine, but I'm seeing some weirdness.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Wait, you flipped DNS already? The health checks were still amber on my dashboard. What happened?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, I got impatient. And of course, traffic hit a cluster that couldn't serve it. Every region is showing elevated error rates right now.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Every region? That's bad. How long has this been going on?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hours. I've been scrambling to roll back, but the damage is done. This is exactly the kind of outage I hate.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Okay, let's fix it first, then we talk about process. But seriously, we need a better way.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Agreed. After this, I'm going to set up health-check-gated DNS failover so traffic auto-routes away from a dead cluster. No more manual judgment calls.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's a solid plan. Let's get through this fire first.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Hey Kim, good news — I waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS this time. The new cluster passed all checks, and I flipped it.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Nice. So traffic moved over without a hitch?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yep, zero errors. It was smooth. I also set up that health-check-gated DNS failover I mentioned — if the cluster dies, traffic auto-routes away.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's great. But I noticed you skipped some flaky tests to make CI green yesterday. I saw the commit message.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah, they were timing out randomly. I figured it was better to get the build passing than to block everyone.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: I get it, but that's risky. Skipping tests can let a regression slip into production. We've seen that before.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I know, I know. But I ran the full regression suite before release — everything passed. So we're good.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Okay, as long as you're running the full suite. Regressions caught before shipping is the goal. Just don't make a habit of skipping.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Fair enough. I'll be more careful.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Kim, I need to tell you something. Remember how I waited for the cluster health check before switching DNS last week? Turns out that wasn't enough.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: What do you mean? It worked perfectly — traffic moved over without a hitch.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: It did, but only because I happened to be paying attention. Yesterday, the health check passed, I switched DNS, and then the cluster degraded five minutes later. We had a mini-outage.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Oh no. So the wait alone didn't protect you.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Exactly. I was wrong about relying on a human to wait. The check is a snapshot, not a guarantee. So I replaced the manual wait with automated health-check-gated DNS — no human can skip the wait, because the system won't switch until the check is green and stays green for a sustained period.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's a big change. So now the DNS failover is fully automated?

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yes. If the cluster fails the check, traffic stays on the old one. If it passes, it switches automatically. No more 'I'll just eyeball it' moments.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: That's the right call. Better than trusting ourselves under pressure.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah. And I also stopped skipping flaky tests — I fixed them instead. Because a regression slipped into production last week from that skipped test, and I don't want that again.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Wait, a regression slipped in? I thought you ran the full suite before release.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: I did, but the flaky test was the one that would have caught it. So now I run the full regression suite every time, no exceptions. Regressions caught before shipping — that's the only way.

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.text: Good. Sounds like you've learned the hard way, but you've got a solid system now.

turns.speaker: Nate
turns.text: Yeah. The old approach fell short, but this new one should hold.
